newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch market set for boost with new "click funds".
newsitem.headline: Dutch market set for boost with new "click funds".

text.p: The Dutch stock market is set for a billion-guilder jamboree in the next couple of weeks with the launch of a series of new index-linked funds known as click funds.
Ruurd Verdam, economic research head at Dutch bank Van Lanschot, said on Friday that tax issues on the funds had been cleared up, making them the latest investor fad.
"Due to clarification on the taxation of the proceeds of such investments, click funds have become extremely popular in the Netherlands," Verdam told an investment seminar.
Tax authorities have made clear that capital gains on these funds, like shares at present, will be exempt from tax.
Click funds are linked to the performance of the AEX index of the top 25 Dutch shares or other indices.
The formula guarantees investors the benefits of a rising index, while their investments are protected from possible big index falls.
Van Lanschot's click fund, to be launched next week with some 200 million guilders ($111.1 million) to invest, has "clicks" at gains of 30, 50 and 70 percent on the AEX.
"Since the level of the AEX at the time of starting the click-fund will be the basis for the promised returns, the money given to us will have to be invested over a very short time," Verdam said.
Verdam said the same was valid for other banks -- ING Bank, Robeco and Generale Bank Nederland -- launching similar funds.
He said the launch of the funds, which are expected to have a combined one billion guilders to invest, added to the Amsterdam Stock Exchange's favourable short-term prospects.
Click-funds guarantee index-linked performance by using different methods.
Van Lanschot plans to buy put options on pre-set AEX levels, guaranteeing investors that any index rise above these levels will be retained to protect against any later index fall.
The bank will use a loan which is to be repaid from the dividend proceeds coming from its AEX share investments.
Verdam said another formula would make fixed-income investments and buy index calls. ($ = 1.800 Dutch Guilders)
